demos.title: The console, and its six games
demos.description: A 4-bit LCD drawn with the token palette: four shades from the unlit segment ghost up to the lit pixel, a side panel with score, best, level and (for Tetris) the next piece, and — on a coarse pointer only — the keypad the original handheld had. Each variant is one game at its opening frame, dealt from a fixed seed.

variants.description: Tetris on its 10x20 panel: the piece, its landing shadow, the next box.
Snake on 20x20 — three segments, one pellet, no next box at all.
Arkanoid: four rows of two-wide bricks, a paddle, one ball.
Racing: two lanes between two dashed verges, the car drawn as the handheld drew it — and its wheels blinking as the road runs.
Tanks: the player's tank in the middle band with its barrel up, the tanks it has left marked above it, and enemies that come in at the corners.
Memory: four 2x2 pads in a d-pad, waiting to light one at a time for the player to repeat.
Three games allowed: the console draws a menu, and the current one is pressed.
The starting level, picked before play with the minus and the plus — the board is dealt again at whatever the person chose.
The paused field wears a clickable veil — and it offers Enter only where Enter actually reaches the console.
The keypad a coarse pointer gets: a four-way pad and OK / Start / Reset, every target at the phone control height, every button carrying its own accessible name.

demos.title: Something to do while you wait
demos.description: <WaitingGame> is one caption and one console. It is controlled by the host's own `active` flag: while the wait is on it plays, and on the edge where the wait ends it unmounts itself — loop, key listener and frames all gone — and calls `onDone` exactly once.

variants.description: Waiting to be admitted to a room, on a phone.
Waiting for an analysis, with three games allowed — the menu is the console's, the caption is the wait's.
The wait ended: `active={false}`, the console is gone, and the card the host owns is all that is left.
